title: Linking messages and form requests
abstract: Studies an organizational setting in which employees describe tasks by email and instant message to specialists who may need follow-up clarification before completing structured forms. A prototype reads communication and assists with the associated task, providing direct evidence of message-to-business-task association across interactive exchanges.
venue: Proceedings of the 11th International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces (IUI 2006)

title: Employing Discourse Coherence Enhancement to Improve Cross-Document Event and Entity Coreference Resolution
abstract: Addresses cross-document coreference where relevant mentions lack a shared coherent document context. The method retrieves additional coherent text, inserts it between mention contexts, and uses the augmented context for event and entity identity decisions, allowing direct evaluation of whether retrieved context improves coreference.
venue: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: An ER-Model-Based Framework for Case Notion Selection in Object-Centric Processes
abstract: Proposes deriving process cases from an entity-relationship schema rather than assuming a single pre-existing case identifier. Cases are constructed from connected components of primary and secondary business entities, making explicit how relational structure induces process-instance identity while avoiding unrestricted resource-based linking.

title: Tracking the Evolution of Clusters in Social Media Streams
abstract: Studies longitudinal cluster evolution in high-volume social-media streams. The framework explicitly tracks cluster emergence, disappearance, adjustment, splitting, and merging, making it useful as transfer evidence for histories in which a persistent grouping can change structure over time.

title: StableID: An Iterative Graph-Based Framework for Persistent Entity Identification in Evolving Industrial Data Systems
abstract: Addresses persistent entity identifiers in evolving industrial data where newly discovered links can merge previously separate graph components and destabilize identifiers. The framework incorporates historical identity information, applies dominance rules during component merges, and aims to preserve stable and auditable identity over time.

title: Surrogate Case Identifier Rules for Construction Site Hoists
abstract: Examines how to construct surrogate process case identifiers when sensor-generated operational events have no native case ID. Multiple candidate case-identification rules are evaluated on a month-long construction-hoist event log, showing that the choice of identity rule can materially alter the resulting process structure.

title: Adaptive online event detection in news streams
abstract: Studies online clustering of news reports that describe the same event. The method adapts event clusters as a stream evolves and includes mechanisms for event merging and noise handling, providing transfer evidence for incremental identity assignment with changing event representations.

title: Enhancing Cross-Document Event Coreference Resolution by Discourse Structure and Semantic Information
abstract: Improves cross-document event coreference by combining semantic event arguments with document-level discourse structure. Features include agents, patients, times, and locations, while rhetorical structure trees and cross-document lexical chains provide longer-range evidence before mention-pair scoring and clustering.

title: Selective Classification Under Distribution Shifts
abstract: Studies classifiers that can abstain on likely errors when deployment distributions differ from training data. It formulates selective classification under label shift, covariate shift, and out-of-distribution inputs and evaluates confidence-score designs intended to preserve useful risk-coverage behavior under such changes.

title: Assessing e-mail intent and tasks in e-mail messages
abstract: Studies work tasks and communicative intent in corporate email using Enron and Avocado data. It develops a task taxonomy and manual annotations and examines how work-related email conversations and tasks develop over time, while also evaluating automatic classification across corporate collections.

title: Cross-document event ordering through temporal, lexical and distributional knowledge
abstract: Studies cross-document event ordering while explicitly addressing event coreference. Event mentions are treated as coreferential when temporal compatibility and semantic compatibility support the same-event interpretation, using lexical and distributional semantic knowledge together with temporal information.

title: Automatically classifying emails into activities
abstract: Studies activity-centered email management and the problem of recognizing whether an incoming email belongs to an ongoing user activity. It evaluates reply-thread and Naive Bayes baselines alongside similarity methods using participants and message content, and combines multiple signals for activity assignment.
venue: Proceedings of the 11th International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces (IUI 2006)

title: Event-Case Correlation for Process Mining using Probabilistic Optimization
abstract: Studies recovery of missing case identifiers from timestamped business-process events. It combines a process model, event attributes, constraints, and probabilistic optimization to assign events to cases, and evaluates multiple similarity measures on real-life datasets.

title: On-Line New Event Detection and Tracking
abstract: Studies strict online decisions about whether each incoming news story belongs to an already observed event or represents a new event. It combines single-pass clustering with threshold-based new-event detection and evaluates adaptive tracking intended to follow events as they evolve.
venue: Proceedings of the 21st Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval

title: Topic Detection and Tracking Evaluation Overview
abstract: Describes the evaluation framework for Topic Detection and Tracking, including topic tracking, link detection, topic detection, first-story detection, and story segmentation. These tasks provide early operational measures for deciding whether arriving news items continue an existing event or initiate a new one.
venue: Topic Detection and Tracking: Event-Based Information Organization

title: Cross-document Event Identity via Dense Annotation
abstract: Focuses explicitly on cross-document event identity and densely annotates related document pairs. The study examines full identity and closely related quasi-identity cases, exposing ambiguities that sparse coreference annotation can miss.
venue: Proceedings of the 25th Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning

title: Using a sledgehammer to crack a nut? Lexical diversity and event coreference resolution
abstract: Examines how lexical diversity affects event coreference and argues that earlier data can make event identity artificially easy when documents within a topic predominantly describe one seminal event. It introduces additional texts containing different instances of similar event types, making false merges between related but distinct events more visible.
venue: Proceedings of the Ninth International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation

title: WEC: Deriving a Large-scale Cross-document Event Coreference dataset from Wikipedia
abstract: Introduces a large-scale English cross-document event-coreference dataset derived from Wikipedia. Unlike datasets restricted to predefined topic clusters, it supports event-identity decisions over a broader document collection and provides a substantially larger training resource.
venue: Proceedings of the 2021 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies

title: Generalizing Cross-Document Event Coreference Resolution Across Multiple Corpora
abstract: Systematically compares cross-document event-coreference methods across several corpora rather than evaluating only in-domain. It shows that cues important for event identity vary across datasets and that neural models may generalize inconsistently, highlighting the danger of transferring benchmark accuracy directly to a different communication domain.

title: First Story Detection In TDT Is Hard
abstract: Examines first-story detection in Topic Detection and Tracking, where an incoming story must be recognized as the first report of a new event rather than a continuation of an existing one. The study highlights the intrinsic difficulty of this online novelty decision.
venue: Proceedings of the Ninth International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management

title: Incremental Multi-source Entity Resolution for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Studies incremental multi-source entity resolution as new source entities are added to existing clusters. It combines efficient assignment with repair operations that can correct erroneous prior clustering decisions and reduce dependence on insertion order.

title: Towards Open World Recognition
abstract: Extends open-set recognition to an open-world setting in which a system must detect unknown classes and later incorporate newly labelled classes. The formulation is relevant to incremental identity systems because it separates recognition of known identities from creation and subsequent learning of new identities.
venue: 2015 IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition

title: Incremental Entity Resolution from Linked Documents
abstract: Studies entity resolution when linked documents are added incrementally rather than processed once in a static batch. Inter-document references and attribute similarity are used so that only a limited affected subset needs to be reconsidered after new data arrives.

title: Probabilistic linkage of large public health data files
abstract: Applies probabilistic record linkage to large data files using field-level agreement evidence and estimated match and nonmatch probabilities. The method operationalizes evidence-based identity decisions when identifiers are imperfect or inconsistent.

title: Revisiting Joint Modeling of Cross-document Entity and Event Coreference Resolution
abstract: Introduces a neural joint model for cross-document entity and event coreference. Mention representations combine lexical context with predicate-argument relationships, enabling entity and event identity decisions to reinforce one another across documents.
venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Develops selective classifiers that abstain on difficult observations so prediction risk can be constrained while retaining as much coverage as possible. The approach provides a practical mechanism for refusing low-confidence identity assignments instead of forcing every item into an existing class.

title: Case notion discovery and recommendation: automated event log building on databases
authors: Wil M. P. van der Aalst
abstract: Addresses construction of process-event logs when an appropriate case notion is not already fixed. It generates candidate case notions, correlates events into traces under those notions, and ranks alternatives, making it relevant to inferring case identity from multi-attribute event data.

title: Cross-document Event Coreference Search: Task, Dataset and Modeling
abstract: Formulates event-coreference search: given an event mention, retrieve mentions elsewhere in a large collection that refer to the same event. The task moves beyond predefined document clusters and tests event identity in a retrieval-scale setting.
venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

title: Multimodal Cross-Document Event Coreference Resolution via Contrastive Evidence Reasoning
abstract: Reframes cross-document event coreference as abductive reasoning between competing same-event and different-event hypotheses. It selects between them using explanatory coherence, parsimony, and consistency, combines multimodal retrieval with incremental graph clustering, and evaluates on ECB+, AIDA Phase 1, and WEC-Eng.

title: A Study of Retrospective and On-Line Event Detection
abstract: Studies retrospective and online event detection in chronologically ordered news, including the online problem of deciding whether incoming material belongs to an already observed event or signals a new one. This provides transferable design evidence for NEW-versus-existing assignment in a stream.

title: Generating Harder Cross-document Event Coreference Resolution Datasets using Metaphoric Paraphrasing
abstract: Introduces ECB+META, a lexically more diverse variant of ECB+ that preserves existing same-event coreference links while paraphrasing event expressions. Experiments show that systems performing strongly on ECB+ degrade on the harder corpus, providing evidence that lexical overlap can exaggerate apparent event-identity performance.

title: Argument centric causal intervention for cross document event coreference resolution
abstract: Targets the binary question of whether cross-document event mentions refer to the same real-world occurrence. The method uses causal intervention and counterfactual trigger perturbations to reduce reliance on superficial lexical matches and isolate evidence contributed by event arguments, with evaluation on ECB+ and GVC.

title: A Two-Stage Classifier with Reject Option for Text Categorisation
abstract: Investigates reject decisions for text categorisation when first-stage evidence is insufficiently reliable. Rejected documents are routed to a second classifier, and the architecture is evaluated on a real Reuters text-categorisation task.
venue: Joint IAPR International Workshops on Structural, Syntactic, and Statistical Pattern Recognition

title: New event detection and topic tracking in Turkish
abstract: Evaluates both detection of first stories for new events and tracking of subsequent stories in a temporally ordered news stream. It also examines combining confidence scores from different similarity measures, making it relevant to evidence fusion for new-versus-existing event decisions.
venue: Journal of the American Society for Information Science and Technology

title: Using Names and Topics for New Event Detection
abstract: Studies new-event detection in chronologically ordered news using separate similarities based on names, topics, and full text. It is useful as transfer evidence that entity names and topical content can contribute to a new-versus-existing decision without themselves defining same-event identity.

title: Detecting Subevent Structure for Event Coreference Resolution
abstract: Separates full event coreference from partial coreference expressed through hierarchical subevent relations. A multiclass model detects subevent relations in addition to full coreference, directly informing the distinction between event identity and part-of relations.

title: Cross-Document Event Coreference Resolution on Discourse Structure
abstract: Treats cross-document event coreference as clustering event mentions that refer to the same real-world events. It introduces document-level rhetorical structure and shortest dependency paths between event mentions to supplement local mention features and evaluates the method on ECB+.

title: Revisiting Joint Modeling of Cross-document Entity and Event Coreference Resolution
abstract: Jointly resolves entity and event coreference across documents using mention spans, surrounding context, and predicate-argument relations. Its analysis on ECB+ finds that the mention span, context, and relations to other mentions all contribute to event-coreference decisions.

title: A Probabilistic Approach to Event-Case Correlation for Process Mining
abstract: Studies how to infer case membership when events collected from different systems lack explicit case identifiers. Its probabilistic optimization maps each event to a case using an underlying process model and temporal behavior, making it transferable to longitudinal work-matter assignment.

title: Event correlation for process discovery from Web service interaction logs
abstract: Addresses correlation of events generated by enterprise applications and Web services when traces are scattered across systems and explicit process-instance identifiers are unavailable. The method determines which events belong to the same execution instance so that business processes can be discovered from distributed logs.

title: Evaluation for Partial Event Coreference
abstract: Distinguishes full event identity from partial event coreference such as subevent and membership relations. It represents partial coreference as directed hierarchical event structure and develops evaluation metrics for systems that predict those structures, explicitly demonstrating that event relations need not be a simple equivalence partition.
venue: Second Workshop on EVENTS: Definition, Detection, Coreference, and Representation

title: Cross-document Event Identity via Dense Annotation
abstract: Directly studies the identity of textual events across different documents and argues that earlier annotation schemes insufficiently address event identity and quasi-identity. Its dense annotation workflow records coreference links together with overlapping contexts such as time, location, and participants, enabling analysis of how those evidence dimensions relate to identity judgments.

title: Conformal selective prediction with cost aware deferral for safe clinical triage under distribution shift
abstract: Combines selective prediction with conformal methods and cost-aware deferral under distribution shift. Although evaluated in clinical triage rather than workplace communication, it provides transferable evidence for allowing uncertain cases to be deferred instead of forcing an identity-like classification when confidence is unreliable.

title: Event Coreference Resolution with their Paraphrases and Argument-aware Embeddings
abstract: Improves event-coreference resolution by incorporating paraphrase information and argument-aware event representations. The approach is relevant to continuity expressed with different wording because it explicitly predicts event identity while using arguments to disambiguate otherwise similar event descriptions.

title: Improving Accuracy and Explainability in Event-Case Correlation via Rule Mining
abstract: Studies event correlation when business-process events lack unique case identifiers and therefore must be grouped into process instances. It introduces rule mining to improve correlation accuracy and explainability, targeting explicit event-to-case identity rather than assuming a correct case ID is already supplied.
venue: IEEE International Conference on Process Mining

title: Step-by-Step Case ID Identification Based on Activity Connection for Cross-Organizational Process Mining
abstract: Studies case identification for cross-organizational process mining where different organizations use independent identifier systems. It incrementally identifies probable case-ID correspondences using connections among activities, providing business-workflow evidence for correlating records that belong to the same distributed process instance.

title: A hybrid learning system for recognizing user tasks from desktop activities and email messages
abstract: Develops a system for associating a knowledge worker's computer activities and email messages with persistent user-defined tasks. The approach combines learned task recognition with information from multiple desktop resources, making it relevant to cross-application work-instance association rather than merely classifying generic activity types.
venue: International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces

title: Post-Hoc Uncertainty Calibration for Domain Drift Scenarios
abstract: Investigates post-hoc confidence calibration when the test distribution drifts away from the calibration distribution. The method perturbs validation data to improve uncertainty estimates under domain shift, providing transferable evidence that IID calibration alone is insufficient for changing streams.

title: Event Coreference Resolution by Iteratively Unfolding Inter-dependencies among Events
abstract: Builds event clusters iteratively while exploiting dependencies within and across event chains. It uses different classifiers for within-document and cross-document links and, after cluster merges, combines arguments from the merged events so that accumulated evidence affects later identity decisions.

title: Improving cross-document event coreference resolution by discourse coherence and structure
abstract: Addresses the lack of coherent shared context between event mentions in different documents. It selects sentences to construct coherent cross-document context, represents that context with discourse structure, and uses the resulting global interaction evidence to resolve event identity; experiments are reported on ECB+ and GVC.

title: A Theory for Record Linkage
abstract: Develops a probabilistic framework for deciding whether pairs of records refer to the same person, object, or event. It formalizes link, non-link, and possible-link decisions while controlling false-link and missed-link error rates, providing a foundational model for evidence combination under uncertain identity.
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

title: Semantic Relations between Events and their Time, Locations and Participants for Event Coreference Resolution
abstract: Examines how event components such as time, location, participants, and other semantic relations contribute to deciding whether event mentions are coreferential. The work directly investigates compatibility evidence that can establish or reject same-event identity rather than relying only on trigger similarity.
